page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading. Hardware cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported processor extensions include AVX, AVX-512, AES, and BMI2.

System memory totals 16.0 GiB, establishing an 8.0 GiB per vCPU ratio aligned with memory-intensive profiles. The instance includes no bundled local storage and requires network-attached volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included and no GPU acceleration available.

Benchmark results reflect the constraints of its single physical core and shared-memory pipeline. The system recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 1052.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 1459.48. Uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth tests yielded 10.38 GB/sec for sequential reads and 9.23 GB/sec for sequential writes. Application-level evaluations showed 1.37 million SET operations per second in Redis and a PassMark database operations metric of 545.78.

From an architectural standpoint, the ecs.se1ne.large trades raw computational throughput for memory capacity. It offers qualitative resource efficiency for services that require elevated RAM footprints without parallel compute pressure. The instance is suited for lightweight caching services, small in-memory databases, staging systems, and low-concurrency memory-bound workloads.
